chunks: From him, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “Indeed, al-Shayṭān blows into the rear of the human being until it is imagined to him that wind has come out from him; and nothing invalidates his wudu (ablution) except wind that he hears or whose smell he finds.”

key_terms.رِيحٌ: wind; passing gas that would invalidate wudu (ablution) if confirmed
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: his wudu (ablution), the state of ritual purity for salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَجِدُ رِيحَهَا: he finds its smell, meaning sensory certainty through odor
key_terms.يَسْمَعُهَا: he hears it, meaning audible certainty of passing wind
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: invalidates or breaks, referring here to wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يُخَيَّلَ: it is made to seem or be imagined, indicating uncertainty rather than certainty
key_terms.ٱلشَّيْطَانَ: Satan, mentioned here as causing baseless misgivings

ai.seo_question: Does doubt about passing wind break wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding doubt in wudu (ablution). It teaches that mere suspicion or sensation does not invalidate ritual purity; rather, certainty is required through hearing the sound or detecting the smell.
